use_cases.name: Password Reset
use_cases.manual_process:
1. User contacts ITSD via call, email, or walk-in to request a password reset.
2. Verifies the user's identity (staff ID, manager confirmation, or security questions).
3. IT agent logs in to Active Directory (AD) and resets the user's password.
4. IT sets a temporary password and forces a reset on next login.
5. IT informs the user of the temporary password and guides them to log in and update it.
6. IT confirms the issue is resolved and closes the ticket.
use_cases.automated_process:
This automation handles password resets by redirecting the requester directly to the Reset Password button, then to the Microsoft 365 portal to complete the process.
Main Flow: 2 Agents
Total: 2 Agents

use_cases.name: Unlock AD Account
use_cases.manual_process:
1.User contacts IT to report their account is locked.
2.IT verifies the user's identity.
3.IT locates the account in Active Directory and unlocks it.
4.IT checks for repeated lockout causes (e.g. cached credentials, old sessions).
5.IT confirms with the user that they can log in successfully.
6.If login still fails, IT resets the password and re-tests.
7.IT closes the ticket once access is restored.
use_cases.automated_process:
This automation detects a locked account and attempts to unlock it automatically, keeping the requester informed throughout. Once unlocked, the user is given the option to also reset their password, in which case NAWA WE redirects them to the Microsoft 365 portal to complete the reset.
Main Flow: 4 Agents
Total: 4 Agents

use_cases.name: Outlook self-healing
use_cases.manual_process:
1.User contacts IT to report an Outlook issue (e.g. not opening, crashing, not syncing).
2.IT remotely connects to the user's machine or provides guided steps.
3.IT runs Outlook in safe mode to isolate the issue.
4.IT repairs the Outlook profile via Mail settings.
5. If repair fails, IT creates a new Outlook profile and reconfigures the mailbox.
6.IT tests Outlook with the user to confirm the issue is resolved.
7.IT closes the ticket once Outlook is functioning normally.
use_cases.automated_process:
This automation resolves Outlook issues by first checking whether the NAWA WE endpoint agent is running. If it is, the self-healing process is initiated and the user is notified upon completion. If the agent is not running, NAWA WE prompts the user to install it and handles the installation automatically on their behalf.
Main Flow: 5 Agents
Total: 5 Agents

use_cases.name: Email group – Creation
use_cases.manual_process:
1.Requester submits a group creation request to ITSD Portal with Line Manager and IT Approver authorisation.
2.IT reviews and confirms all required approvals are in place.
3.IT creates the distribution group in the mail management system with the required name and email address.
4.IT adds the initial members as listed in the request.
5.IT sets the group owner and configures send permissions.
6.IT sends a test email to verify the group is working.
7.IT notifies the requester and closes the ticket.
use_cases.automated_process:
This automation manages the creation of email distribution groups. NAWA WE presents the Group Distribution Request options (Create, Add, Remove), directs the requester to the Creation Request form, and generates a ticket confirmation upon submission. Approval notifications are sent to the Line Manager and then IT Management, with the requester kept informed at each stage. Once fully approved, NAWA WE provisions the group and sends the distribution list email address to the requester.
Rejected: NAWA WE notifies the requester of the rejection and cancels the ticket.
Missed Approval: If an approver does not respond, NAWA WE automatically sends follow-up reminders up to 7 times until a response is received.
Failed: If the request fails after both approvals, the ticket is marked as Failed and assigned to an IT Engineer.
Main Flow: 9 Agents
Rejected: 7 Agents
Missed: 12 Agents
Failed: 10 Agents
Total: 38 Agents

use_cases.name: Printer installation
use_cases.manual_process:
1. User contacts or raised ticket to ITSD Portal to request printer installation.
2. Given the confirmed the printer model and the user's device details.
3. IT remotely connects to the user's machine or visits in person.
4. IT installs the correct printer driver and adds the printer via the network path or IP address.
5. IT prints a test page to confirm installation is successful.
6. If installation fails, IT checks network connectivity, driver compatibility, and firewall settings, then retries or escalates.
7. IT confirms with the user and closes the ticket.
use_cases.automated_process:
This automation installs printers by first verifying that the NAWA WE endpoint agent is running on the user's device. Once confirmed, NAWA WE initiates the printer mapping and installation process and notifies the user upon successful completion.
Failed: If the installation fails, NAWA WE automatically creates a support ticket, assigns it to an IT Engineer, and notifies the requester with the ITSD ticket reference.
Main Flow: 4 Agents
Failed: 4 Agents
Total: 8 Agents

4. IT provides the code to the user and closes the ticket.

use_cases.name: Color Printer Access

This automation grants colour printing access by checking whether the requester already has a printer code. If no code exists, NAWA WE generates one and assigns colour access. If a grayscale-only code already exists, NAWA WE upgrades it to include colour access. In both cases, the requester receives a confirmation with the printer code and access details.

use_cases.name: Software installation
use_cases.manual_process:
1.User or manager submits a software request to ITSD Portal with business justification and Line Manager approval.
2.IT confirms IT Approver authorisation and checks licence availability.
3.IT remotely connects to the user's machine or deploys via the software management system.
4.IT installs the approved software and performs a basic functionality check.
5. For licensed software, IT registers the licence in the software asset register.
6.If installation fails, IT checks system requirements and compatibility, then retries or escalates.
7.IT confirms with the user and closes the ticket.
use_cases.automated_process:
NAWA WE routes the requester through a software selection form and sends the request for Line Manager approval. Once approved, non-licensed software is installed immediately and the requester is notified.
Licensed: Once approved, NAWA WE closes the request, provides the material code, and advises the requester to coordinate with Procurement for licence purchase.
Failed: If installation fails after approval, NAWA WE raises a support ticket, assigns it to an IT Engineer, and shares the ticket number with the requester.
Non-Licensed: 5 Agents
Licensed: 5 Agents
Failed: 4 Agents
Total: 14 Agents

use_cases.name: Windows Update Installation
use_cases.manual_process:
1. User raises a ticket through the ITSD portal requesting a Windows update installation.
2. IT identifies the device and verifies pending updates via the patch management system.
3. IT schedules the update during off-peak hours or coordinates with the user.
4. IT pushes the update remotely or guides the user to run it manually.
5. IT confirms successful completion and closes the ticket.
6. If the update fails, IT investigates the error, resolves compatibility issues, and retries
use_cases.automated_process:
NAWA WE initiates pending Windows updates on the user's device and runs the installation automatically in the background without any user interaction required.
If Failed: If the installation fails, NAWA WE automatically triggers an ITSD ticket and assigns it to an IT Engineer to perform the update manually. Once completed, the user is notified that the ticket has been closed.
Main Flow: — Agents
Completed: 1
Failed: 2
Total: 3 Agents

For IT-related tickets, NAWA WE generates an ITSD ticket and assigns it directly to the ITSD bin for re-assignment to the relevant team. use_cases.name: T&A device proactive detection of failure.
use_cases.manual_process:
1.Users raise tickets after they realize missing attendance for at least 2-4 days.
2. I check their employee ID to find which device is offline
3. If the site has IT, we notify site IT/Admin to get the device back online or reply to the user that the device is offline.
4. User gets back later once device internet is fixed,
5. I fetch the attendance data from the day it went offline
6. Run the program that Kamal created to push the data to SAP.
7. Informs user that the attendance will reflect on next day by 2.30pm, or re-assigns the ticket to SAP team so that they'll run their program and replicates the attendance
use_cases.automated_process: Email notifications are sent to the concerned team for attendance machines that are detected as offline.

use_cases.name: Proactive Validation of Data Sync with DB/SAP
use_cases.manual_process:
1. Employee reports missing attendance in SAP via ticket, Teams, or email.
2.IT retrieves the employee ID and runs it through the application to locate the attendance data.
3. IT validates whether the attendance records exist in the system.
If Attendance Data is Not Available
4. IT checks the T&A device status (online/offline).
5 If the device is offline, IT supports getting it back online and waits for the data to upload.
6. Once data is uploaded, IT runs the program to push the attendance data to SAP.
7. IT notifies the employee that the attendance will be reflected by the next day at 2: 30 PM, or notifies the SAP team to run their replication program, or re-assgin the ticket to SAP Team with the remarks that the data is pushed
8. If Attendance Data is Available but Reflected Late
9. IT runs the program to push the attendance data to SAP.
10. IT notifies the SAP team to update the attendance accordingly.
use_cases.automated_process: Validate attendance data in the database and SAP; if any records are missing, automatically push the missing entries to DB.

use_cases.name: Automation Dashboard Data Extractor
use_cases.manual_process:
1. IT logs in to the automation dashboard.
2. IT navigates to the reporting or analytics section.
3. IT applies the date filter and selects the "Till Now" option to capture all data from the start up to the current date.
4. IT selects each active use case individually to generate the corresponding report.
5.IT extracts and saves the report for each active use case.
6. IT reviews the extracted data to ensure completeness and accuracy.
use_cases.automated_process: Pulling data from the automation dashboard and adding it to the IT Database.
